name: Topic 30: Daily water requirement
defaultTargetFormula: target_ml = base(sex: male 2500, female 2000, unknown 2500) + clamp((weight_kg - ref_weight) * 20, -400, 400) + min(workout_minutes * 8, 1000) + (hot_weather ? 500 : 0) + (pregnant ? 300 : 0) + (lactating ? 700 : 0); ref_weight male 65 kg, female 55 kg; clamp result 1500-4500 ml; round to nearest 50 ml. Drinks only; base uses EFSA 2010 total-water AI (2.5 / 2.0 L); pregnancy/lactation add-ons from EFSA 2010; other slopes are FitPlate estimates (est.). ICMR-NIN 2020 water values Not found.

reminderRules.rule: Up to 6 reminders per day at about 09:30, 11:30, 13:30, 15:30, 17:30, 19:30, each prompting about 250 ml (est.)
reminderRules.source: FitPlate design (est.); drink-to-thirst / heat advisory context from NDMA and EAH consensus 2015

reminderRules.rule: Skip a reminder if a drink was logged in the last 60 minutes; stop when target is reached; none after 21:00 (est.)
Add one extra reminder on hot-weather or workout days
Users aged 60+: keep scheduled reminders even if not thirsty
reminderRules.source: Reviews on reduced thirst in older adults (PMC); EFSA 2010 same AI for elderly

reminderRules.rule: Doctor-flag users (kidney, heart, liver, fluid limit, diuretics): no hydration reminders; show 'Follow your doctor's fluid advice'
reminderRules.source: FitPlate safety design; Topic 18 and Topic 19 convention

warnings: No upper limit is set for healthy adults, but forced over-drinking can cause low blood sodium; drink to thirst during long exercise.
Users with kidney, heart or liver disease, fluid limits, diuretics, or pregnancy with swelling or high BP: show only 'Follow your doctor's advice'; no push to drink more.
Older adults: thirst is weaker; sip regularly unless a doctor has limited fluids.
ICMR-NIN 2020 water values Not found; the app default is a FitPlate estimate built on EFSA and NASEM adequate intakes.
ORS is for illness, not for daily use.
